subject.title: feat(gateway): retain trusted-proxy verified identity on the connection for per-user session scoping (+ expose it on pairing requests)

question: Should one OpenClaw gateway support multiple authenticated user principals, and what canonical ownership source, administrator behavior, shared-session classes, privacy rules, and backward-compatible default should define that boundary?
rationale: Current main proves the identity primitive is missing, but adopting it creates a new tenancy, configuration, protocol, privacy, and authorization contract that cannot be selected safely from source evidence alone.

options.title: Design generic principal boundary
options.body: Define a transport-independent server principal and one centralized authorization policy that supports trusted proxy and future token or service identities.

options.title: Retain principal only
options.body: Preserve verified identity and expose it for pairing and audit consumers while deferring session isolation to separately sponsored work.

options.title: Keep single-operator gateways
options.body: Decline in-gateway multi-user tenancy and require isolated gateway instances or an external authorization control plane.

recommendation.title: Design generic principal boundary
recommendation.body: Define a transport-independent server principal and one centralized authorization policy that supports trusted proxy and future token or service identities.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced trusted-proxy mode and reviewed its original security semantics, making them the strongest feature-history owner for the principal-boundary decision.
